params.body:
Two things a writer could not do in the editor.

## The Opportunity from the conversation

- A suggestion for the Opportunity (pipeline PR alongside) shows in the Opportunity section, not in the text. It reads as the heading and paragraph would, with Accept, Dismiss, and Previous / Next / Another between versions.
- Accepting fills the Opportunity's two fields in the editor.
- The section opens as soon as there is such a suggestion, even before the piece has grown.

## Who a post is about, in the margin

- Topics, generations, life stages and regions were set only by import and runs. The editor did not show them, while they drive the filters on gentells.com.
- "Who it is about" sits in the margin between the sources and the elements. Each tag is text that is on (underlined) or off, and a click saves.
- Cohorts keep the Gentells Standard's pairs (`toggleCohort` in `piece.js`): Tweens brings Kids, removing Kids removes Tweens, and ZAlpha needs Gen Z or Gen Alpha. Removing the last of those removes ZAlpha. A pairing the Standard refuses would hold a live post back from the site.
- Proposed life stages show only when a piece already carries one.
- The lists come from the pipeline's `/taxonomy`, which already sent them.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 48 pass, including the cohort pairs. `vite build` is clean.
- Checked in a local Studio against a copy of production: an Opportunity suggestion accepted into the fields, and Tweens bringing Kids, both saved.
params.title: Opportunity suggestions, and who a post is about in the margin
